title: Shrinking a local inverse chart to a coordinate square
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, M, U, N₀ ⊆ ℝ^P, O ⊆ ℝ² (Euclid 2), F : ℝ^P → ℝ², G : ℝ² → ℝ^P, p ∈ ℝ^P and r₀ > 0. Assume U is open, F is continuous on U, O and N₀ are open, F(p) = (r₀, 0), F(p) ∈ O, p ∈ N₀ ⊆ U, G(O) = M ∩ N₀ and F(G(w)) = w for all w ∈ O. For s ∈ ℝ let R_s := {w ∈ ℝ² : w₀ ∈ (r₀ − s, r₀ + s), w₁ ∈ (−s, s)}. Then there are s ∈ ℝ with 0 < s < r₀ and an open set N ⊆ ℝ^P with p ∈ N ⊆ U, R_s ⊆ O and M ∩ N = G(R_s).
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M U N₀ : Set (Euclid P)) (O : Set (Euclid 2)) (F : Euclid P → Euclid 2) (G : Euclid 2 → Euclid P) (p : Euclid P) (r₀ : ℝ), 0 < r₀ → IsOpen U → ContinuousOn F U → IsOpen O → IsOpen N₀ → F p = !₂[r₀, 0] → F p ∈ O → p ∈ N₀ → N₀ ⊆ U → G '' O = M ∩ N₀ → (∀ w ∈ O, F (G w) = w) → ∃ (s : ℝ) (N : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < s ∧ s < r₀ ∧ IsOpen N ∧ p ∈ N ∧ N ⊆ U ∧ {w : Euclid 2 | w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ∧ w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s} ⊆ O ∧ M ∩ N = G '' {w : Euclid 2 | w 0 ∈ Ioo (r₀ - s) (r₀ + s) ∧ w 1 ∈ Ioo (-s) s}
